delighted.definition: very pleased or happy about something.
examples: She was delighted to win the prize.

daughter.definition: a female child in relation to her parents.

difficult.definition: not easy to do or understand.

examples: The drum is loud in this band.

desk.definition: a piece of furniture with a flat surface for writing or reading.
examples: Her desk is tidy.

dress.definition: a one-piece garment for women or girls; clothing in general.

dangerous.definition: able to cause harm or injury; not safe.
examples: The road is dangerous at night.

drama.definition: a play for theater, television, or film; a real-life event that is dramatic.

designing.definition: Describing something that involves planning and creating; used to describe processes or activities related to planning.

designed.definition: Past tense of the verb meaning to plan and create something.

designed.definition: Made or created according to a plan or specification; intended.

design-ing.definition: The act of planning and creating something, especially a plan or drawings.

design-ing.definition: To plan and create the form, structure, or appearance of something.

droll.definition: Amusing in a dry or odd way; pleasantly humorous.
examples: His droll comments lightened the mood in the meeting.

dalmatic.definition: a long ceremonial vestment worn by clergy in some Christian traditions
examples: The bishop wore a dalmatic during the ceremony.

dog.definition: a common pet animal with fur that often barks
examples: Our dog loves walks.
The dog is friendly.

dexterous.definition: good at using your hands or moving skillfully, especially in tasks requiring skill
examples: The surgeon was dexterous.
He is dexterous with tools.

defenestrate.definition: to throw someone or something out of a window
examples: The story says they tried to defenestrate the prisoner.

describe.definition: to explain or give details about something
examples: Can you describe what happened?
She described the house in detail.

dude.definition: a man, often used in informal speech
examples: That dude over there is my cousin.
Hey dude, what’s going on?

dawn.definition: the time of day when the sun starts to rise
examples: We left at dawn.
The sky turned orange at dawn.

dusk.definition: the time in the evening when daylight is ending
examples: We arrived at dusk.
The birds went quiet at dusk.

dope.definition: a drug that is illegal or harmful

dope.definition: to add drugs to something or to drug someone

dope.definition: excellent or exciting in informal speech

dreary.definition: gray, dull, or depressing, making you feel unhappy
examples: The weather was dreary all day.
The office felt dreary.

dingy.definition: dirty or looking dull and not clean
examples: The apartment looked dingy.
The hallway was dingy and quiet.

dawg.definition: informal slang for dog or for a friend, depending on context
examples: My dawg is outside.
That dawg can cook!

doctor.definition: a person who is trained to treat illnesses and injuries
examples: The doctor said it was not serious.
I have an appointment with a doctor.

doggedly.definition: In a stubborn and determined way, even when it is difficult
examples: He kept asking doggedly until he got an answer.
She worked doggedly through the late evening to finish the report.

dismal.definition: Very gloomy or depressing, or of poor quality
examples: The weather was dismal all week.
His performance was dismal compared to last year.

doubt.definition: Uncertainty about whether something is true or right
examples: There is some doubt about the accuracy of the report.
She has no doubt that she can do it.

doubt.definition: To feel uncertain or not believe something is true
examples: I doubt that he will be on time.
Many people doubt the results.
She dashed to the door when the phone rang.
They dashed across the street to avoid the rain.

dash.definition: A quick run or short burst of movement
examples: He took a dash to the store before dinner.
We made a dash for the exit.

decode.definition: To change coded information into a form that can be understood
examples: They decoded the message using a new key.
Can you decode this data format?

decipher.definition: To figure out the meaning of something that is difficult to understand
examples: She deciphered the handwriting after many attempts.
The scientist helped decipher the ancient text.

dread.definition: A strong feeling of fear that something unpleasant will happen
examples: She felt dread before the exam.
There was a sense of dread in the room.

dread.definition: To feel afraid that something unpleasant will happen
examples: He dreaded the meeting because of the criticism.
I dread having to call them.

dimmed.definition: Made less bright or less clear
examples: The lights were dimmed in the evening.
Her smile dimmed when the news arrived.

doubtful.definition: Uncertain; likely not true or not expected
examples: I’m doubtful that we’ll finish on time.
The evidence is doubtful.

diminish.definition: To become smaller or less intense
examples: The pain diminished after the medicine.
Traffic noise diminishes at night.

decline.definition: To become less; to get worse or smaller over time
examples: Sales declined after the price increase.
Her health began to decline in winter.

decline.definition: A decrease in something such as quality, quantity, or health
examples: There was a decline in customer satisfaction.
The decline in costs improved profits.

demand.definition: To ask for something strongly or officially
examples: They demanded an explanation from the manager.
The law demands that vehicles stop at the sign.

demand.definition: A strong need or request for something
examples: There is high demand for skilled workers.
The demand for new housing has increased.

desolate.definition: Empty, lonely, and without comfort or hope
examples: The street looked desolate after midnight.
They lived in a desolate area with few services.

dodgy.definition: Unreliable, suspicious, or of low quality
examples: That used car deal sounds dodgy.
Be careful with dodgy websites.

dubious.definition: Not confident that something is true or good; doubtful
examples: I’m dubious about the results because they lack evidence.
The website looks dubious.

decay.definition: The process of becoming worse or breaking down over time
examples: The decay of the building started after years without repairs.
Fungi can speed up decay.

decay.definition: To break down or become worse over time
examples: The fruit began to decay in the heat.
The metal will decay if it is not protected.
His health deteriorated rapidly.
The roads deteriorate after the winter season.

didactic.definition: Teaching in a way that is meant to instruct or explain moral or learning lessons
examples: The didactic style helped students understand the topic.
His speech became didactic and repetitive.

discern.definition: To notice or understand something that is not obvious
examples: I could discern a change in her voice.
The report helps you discern key trends.

distinguish.definition: To recognize the difference between two things
examples: It’s hard to distinguish the two models.
The test helps distinguish between similar diseases.

decide.definition: To make a choice after thinking about something
examples: We need to decide by Friday.
She decided to study abroad.

determine.definition: To find out or decide something after careful thinking or research
examples: The team determined the cause of the delay.
We must determine which option is best.

debt.definition: Money that one person or organization owes to another
examples: He is trying to pay off his debt.
The company has a large debt.

diagnosis.definition: The process of identifying what illness or condition a person has
examples: The diagnosis was made after several tests.
Her diagnosis came as a surprise to the family.

dialogue.definition: A conversation between two or more people
examples: We need better dialogue between management and employees.
The book includes a dialogue between two characters.

dialogue.definition: In writing, the spoken lines of characters
examples: The dialogue sounded natural.
The dialogue in the movie was well written.
